SOUTH AFRICA FREELANCER TAX SET-ASIDE · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER · NOTHING UPLOADED

How much of what you earn should you set aside for tax?

Enter your business income and expenses. You get income tax after rebates and medical credits, a provisional tax guide, and the share of every invoice to put away.

Written from the published SARS 2025/26 tables (1 March 2025 to 28 February 2026) without a live lookup; 2026/27 figures may differ slightly. SARS decides. Not tax advice.

What it does, and what it leaves to you

    
    
      
  • Covers: SARS's sliding-scale income tax from 18% to 45%, the primary, secondary and tertiary age rebates, medical scheme fees tax credits, the retirement annuity deduction (27.5% of profit, capped at R350,000), and a provisional tax and VAT registration guide.
    • 
      
  • Not decided: interest, dividends, capital gains, rental or employment income, home office and travel deductions, the additional medical expenses credit, VAT amounts, non-residents, and exactly how much provisional tax you must pay. SARS or your tax practitioner decides these.
    • 
    

  


  

    
Common questions

    
How much of my freelance income should I set aside for tax in South Africa?

    
Often 15% to 30% of profit, depending on how much you earn: SARS taxes personal income on a sliding scale from 18% to 45%. Enter your income and expenses here for a number built from the actual brackets, rebates and medical credits.

    
What is provisional tax?

    
The way freelancers and other people with untaxed income pay SARS during the year: two compulsory payments, about half the estimated tax by the end of August and the balance by the last day of February, plus an optional top-up after year end.

    
Do I pay UIF as a freelancer?

    
No. UIF and SDL are employer and employee levies. A self-employed person pays income tax on profit and, when registered, VAT.

    
When must I register for VAT?

    
Compulsorily when taxable turnover exceeds R1 million in any 12 months; voluntarily once it exceeds R50,000. VAT you collect belongs to SARS, so keep it out of your set-aside.

    
Is my data uploaded anywhere?

    
No. Everything is calculated in your browser and nothing is sent.
